definitions.explanation: Designating something modeled on Western (especially European or American) conventions, in contrast to {日本式|にほんしき} or {和式|わしき} (Japanese-style).

examples.japanese: {西洋式|せいようしき}のトイレ。
{西洋式|せいようしき}の{食事|しょくじ}に{慣|な}れてきた。
examples.english: I've gotten used to Western-style meals.

examples.japanese: {明治時代|めいじじだい}に、{西洋式|せいようしき}の{建築|けんちく}が{多|おお}く{導入|どうにゅう}された。
examples.english: In the Meiji era, many Western-style buildings were introduced.

notes:
Compound of {西洋|せいよう} (the West) + the suffix {式|しき} (style, system). The {式|しき} suffix produces many style/type words: {日本式|にほんしき} (Japanese-style), {新式|しんしき} (new style), {結婚式|けっこんしき} (wedding ceremony).

GRAMMAR:
- As a noun modifier: {西洋式|せいようしき}の + noun
- As a predicate: {西洋式|せいようしき}だ / です

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {洋式|ようしき}: Western-style — shorter, more common in everyday contexts (especially {洋式|ようしき}トイレ)
- {西洋|せいよう}{風|ふう}: Western in feel — softer; emphasizes a Western-like atmosphere rather than strict conformity
- {欧米式|おうべいしき}: European/American style — narrower; specifies Europe and North America
